scenario: A bank treasury analyst uses an automated pipeline to produce the monthly Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) regulatory stress report. The pipeline reads the bank's High-Quality Liquid Asset (HQLA) position file (CSV), normalises units for each asset's run-off rate, applies Basel III haircuts to compute the adjusted HQLA stock, aggregates 30-day net cash outflows, computes LCR = Adjusted HQLA / Net Cash Outflows, and writes a formatted LCR report to be submitted to the prudential regulator.
info_flow: csv-pipeline reads the HQLA position CSV and enriches each row with a tier classification and haircut rate → unit-convert normalises the outflow stress-rate percentages to decimals → financial-calculator applies haircuts to each asset, sums the adjusted HQLA stock, aggregates net cash outflows, divides to produce the LCR ratio, and outputs the regulatory report.
